# tempfile - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tempfile/^3.26/

## Expand description

This is a library for creating temporary files and directories that are automatically deleted when no longer referenced (i.e., on drop).

- Use `tempfile()``std::fs::File`
- Use `NamedTempFile::new()`*named*temporary file that can be referred to its path.
- Use `tempdir()`
- Use `spooled_tempfile()`

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

This crate provides several approaches to creating temporary files and directories.
[ tempfile()](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) relies on the OS to remove the temporary file once the last handle is closed.

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`[both rely on Rust destructors for cleanup.](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[§](https://docs.rs#resource-leaking)Resource Leaking

`tempfile` will (almost) never fail to cleanup temporary resources. However `TempDir` and
`NamedTempFile` will fail if their destructors don’t run. This is because `tempfile` relies on
the OS to cleanup the underlying file, while `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on rust
destructors to do so. Destructors may fail to run if the process exits through an unhandled
signal interrupt (like `SIGINT`), or if the instance is declared statically (like with
[ lazy_static](https://github.com/rust-lang-nursery/lazy-static.rs/issues/62)), among other possible reasons.

[§](https://docs.rs#unexpected-file-deletion)Unexpected File Deletion

Most operating systems periodically clean up temporary files that haven’t been accessed recently
(often on the order of multiple days). This issue does not affect unnamed temporary files but
can invalidate the paths associated with named temporary files on Unix-like systems because the
temporary file can be unlinked from the filesystem while still open and in-use. See the
[temporary file cleaner](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners) section for more security implications.

[§](https://docs.rs#security)Security

This section discusses security issues relevant to Unix-like operating systems that use shared temporary directories by default. Importantly, it’s not relevant for Windows or macOS as both operating systems use private per-user temporary directories by default.

Applications can mitigate the issues described below by using [ env::override_temp_dir](https://docs.rs/env/fn.override_temp_dir.html) to
change the default temporary directory but should do so if and only if default the temporary
directory (

[) is unsuitable (is world readable, world writable, managed by a temporary file cleaner, etc.).](https://docs.rs/env/fn.temp_dir.html)

`env::temp_dir`[§](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners)Temporary File Cleaners

In the presence of pathological temporary file cleaner, relying on file paths is unsafe because a temporary file cleaner could delete the temporary file which an attacker could then replace.

This isn’t an issue for [ tempfile](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) as it doesn’t rely on file paths. However,

[and temporary directories](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`*do*rely on file paths for

*some*operations. See the security documentation on the

[and the](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[types for more information.](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`Mitigation:

- This is rarely an issue for short-lived files as temporary file cleaners usually only remove temporary files that haven’t been modified or accessed within many (10-30) days.
- Very long lived temporary files should be placed in directories not managed by temporary file cleaners.

[§](https://docs.rs#access-permissions)Access Permissions

Temporary *files* created with this library are private by default on all operating systems.
However, temporary *directories* are created with the default permissions and will therefore be
world-readable by default unless the user has changed their umask and/or default temporary
directory.

[§](https://docs.rs#denial-of-service)Denial of Service

If the file-name randomness ([ Builder::rand_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.rand_bytes)) is too small and/or this crate is built
without the

`getrandom` feature, it may be possible for an attacker to predict the random file
names chosen by this library, preventing temporary file creation by creating temporary files
with these predicted file names. By default, this library mitigates this denial of service
attack by:- Defaulting to 6 random characters per temporary file forcing an attacker to create billions of files before random collisions are expected (at which point you probably have larger problems).
- Re-seeding the random filename generator from system randomness after 3 failed attempts to
create temporary a file (when the `getrandom`feature is enabled as it is by default on all major platforms).

[§](https://docs.rs#early-drop-pitfall)Early drop pitfall

Because `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on their destructors for cleanup, this can lead
to an unexpected early removal of the directory/file, usually when working with APIs which are
generic over `AsRef<Path>`. Consider the following example:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::process::Command;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let temp_dir = tempdir()?;
// Spawn the `touch` command inside the temporary directory and collect the exit status
// Note that `temp_dir` is **not** moved into `current_dir`, but passed as a reference
let exit_status = Command::new("touch").arg("tmp").current_dir(&temp_dir).status()?;
assert!(exit_status.success());
```
This works because a reference to `temp_dir` is passed to `current_dir`, resulting in the
destructor of `temp_dir` being run after the `Command` has finished execution. Moving the
`TempDir` into the `current_dir` call would result in the `TempDir` being converted into
an internal representation, with the original value being dropped and the directory thus
being deleted, before the command can be executed.

The `touch` command would fail with an `No such file or directory` error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a temporary file and write some data into it:

```
use tempfile::tempfile;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file = tempfile()?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
```
Create a named temporary file and open an independent file handle:

```
use tempfile::NamedTempFile;
use std::io::{Write, Read};
let text = "Brian was here. Briefly.";
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file1 = NamedTempFile::new()?;
// Re-open it.
let mut file2 = file1.reopen()?;
// Write some test data to the first handle.
file1.write_all(text.as_bytes())?;
// Read the test data using the second handle.
let mut buf = String::new();
file2.read_to_string(&mut buf)?;
assert_eq!(buf, text);
```
Create a temporary directory and add a file to it:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let dir = tempdir()?;
let file_path = dir.path().join("my-temporary-note.txt");
let mut file = File::create(file_path)?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
// By closing the `TempDir` explicitly, we can check that it has
// been deleted successfully. If we don't close it explicitly,
// the directory will still be deleted when `dir` goes out
// of scope, but we won't know whether deleting the directory
// succeeded.
drop(file);
dir.close()?;
```

See libc(3LIB) on Solaris or illumos: https://illumos.org/man/3lib/libc https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E36784_01/html/E36873/libc-3lib.html https://www.unix.com/man-page/opensolaris/3LIB/libc/

# bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/target-redirect/bevy_dlc/

Registry for encrypt keys and DLC asset paths. This tracks which encrypt key is
associated with which DLC id, and which asset paths are associated with which DLC id
so that they can be reloaded when the DLC is unlocked.

Defines a simple “text-like” asset type along with a loader and a Bevy
plugin for it. The generated loader reads the file as UTF-8 and stores a
String in the asset. The plugin registers the loader and the DLC type.

Builds a Vec<PackItem> from a list of entries. Each entry specifies a
path and its raw contents; optional query-style suffixes allow specifying an
explicit original extension or a type path as well.

Represents a single encrypted file inside a .dlcpack container, along with its metadata (DLC ID, original extension, optional type path). The ciphertext is not decrypted at this stage; decryption is performed on demand by DlcPackEntry::decrypt_bytes using the global encrypt key registry.

Compression level for packing. Controls the trade-off between pack size and packing time.
Higher levels produce smaller files but take longer to create.
TODO: v6 format will allow a pack to contain multiple blocks with different compression levels, because some file types compress better than others.

Parse a .dlcpack container and return product, embedded dlc_id, and a list
of (path, EncryptedAsset) pairs. For v3 format, also validates the signature
against the authorized product public key.

Extract the embedded encryption key from a signed license’s payload (base64url-encoded).
Returns None if the token is malformed or contains no encrypt_key.

Lazy hash set used by [is_forbidden_extension].
Simple heuristic used by the packer to detect executable payloads. It is
intentionally forgiving; the goal is merely to catch obvious binaries when
a user accidentally tries to pack them.

Parse the binary encrypted-asset format from a byte slice. This is used by the pack loader when parsing the pack metadata, and also by the DlcLoader when decrypting individual entries (since the entry metadata is stored in the same format as a standalone encrypted file).

Register an encryption key for a DLC ID in the global registry.
This is used internally by the plugin and can be called by tools/CLI for key management.

A secure wrapper for a 32-byte Ed25519 signing seed (private key) used to create signed licenses. This should be protected and never exposed in logs or error messages.

---

[261](#261)pub fn extract_encrypt_key_from_license(license: &SignedLicense) -> Option<EncryptionKey> {
[264](#264)    license.with_secret(|token_str| {
[265](#265)        let parts: Vec<&str> = token_str.split('.').collect();
[266](#266)        if parts.len() != 2 {
[267](#267)            return None;
[268](#268)        }
[269](#269)        let payload = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(parts[0].as_bytes()).ok()?;

[377](#377)impl DlcKey {
[378](#378)    pub fn new(pubkey: &str, privkey: &str) -> Result<Self, DlcError> {
[379](#379)        let decoded_pub = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
[380](#380)            .decode(pubkey.as_bytes())
[381](#381)            .map_err(|e| DlcError::CryptoError(format!("invalid pubkey base64: {}", e)))?;
[382](#382)        if decoded_pub.len() != 32 {
[383](#383)            return Err(DlcError::CryptoError("public key must be 32 bytes".into()));
[384](#384)        }
[385](#385)        let mut pub_bytes = [0u8; 32];
[386](#386)        pub_bytes.copy_from_slice(&decoded_pub);
[387](#387)
[388](#388)        let decoded_priv = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
[389](#389)            .decode(privkey.as_bytes())
[390](#390)            .map_err(|e| DlcError::CryptoError(format!("invalid privkey base64: {}", e)))?;
[391](#391)        if decoded_priv.len() != 32 {
[392](#392)            return Err(DlcError::CryptoError("private key must be 32 bytes".into()));
[393](#393)        }
[394](#394)        let mut priv_bytes = [0u8; 32];
[395](#395)        priv_bytes.copy_from_slice(&decoded_priv);
[396](#396)
[397](#397)        Self::from_priv_and_pub(PrivateKey::from(priv_bytes), PublicKey(pub_bytes))
[398](#398)    }
[399](#399)
[400](#400)    pub fn public(pubkey: &str) -> Result<Self, DlcError> {
[402](#402)        let decoded_pub = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
[403](#403)            .decode(pubkey.as_bytes())
[404](#404)            .map_err(|e| DlcError::CryptoError(format!("invalid pubkey base64: {}", e)))?;
[405](#405)        if decoded_pub.len() != 32 {
[406](#406)            return Err(DlcError::CryptoError("public key must be 32 bytes".into()));
[407](#407)        }
[408](#408)        let mut pub_bytes = [0u8; 32];
[409](#409)        pub_bytes.copy_from_slice(&decoded_pub);
[410](#410)
[411](#411)        Ok(DlcKey::Public {
[412](#412)            pubkey: PublicKey(pub_bytes),
[413](#413)        })
[414](#414)    }
[415](#415)
[416](#416)    pub(crate) fn from_priv_and_pub(
[418](#418)        privkey: PrivateKey,
[419](#419)        publickey: PublicKey,
[420](#420)    ) -> Result<Self, DlcError> {
[421](#421)        let kp = privkey
[422](#422)            .with_secret(|priv_bytes| {
[423](#423)                Ed25519KeyPair::from_seed_and_public_key(priv_bytes, &publickey.0)
[424](#424)            })
[425](#425)            .map_err(|e| DlcError::CryptoError(format!("invalid seed: {:?}", e)))?;
[426](#426)        let mut pub_bytes = [0u8; 32];
[427](#427)        pub_bytes.copy_from_slice(kp.public_key().as_ref());
[428](#428)
[429](#429)        privkey
[430](#430)            .with_secret(|priv_bytes| {
[431](#431)                Ed25519KeyPair::from_seed_and_public_key(priv_bytes, &pub_bytes)
[432](#432)            })
[433](#433)            .map_err(|e| DlcError::CryptoError(format!("keypair validation failed: {:?}", e)))?;
[434](#434)
[435](#435)        Ok(DlcKey::Private {
[436](#436)            privkey,
[437](#437)            pubkey: PublicKey(pub_bytes),
[438](#438)        })
[439](#439)    }
[440](#440)
[441](#441)    pub fn generate_random() -> Self {
[445](#445)        let privkey: PrivateKey = PrivateKey::new(rand::random());
[446](#446)
[447](#447)        let pair = privkey
[448](#448)            .with_secret(|priv_bytes| Ed25519KeyPair::from_seed_unchecked(priv_bytes))
[449](#449)            .expect("derive public key from seed");
[450](#450)        let mut pub_bytes = [0u8; 32];
[451](#451)        pub_bytes.copy_from_slice(pair.public_key().as_ref());
[452](#452)
[453](#453)        Self::from_priv_and_pub(privkey, PublicKey(pub_bytes))
[454](#454)            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("generate_complete failed: {:?}", e))
[455](#455)    }

[457](#457)    pub fn get_public_key(&self) -> &PublicKey {
[458](#458)        match self {
[459](#459)            DlcKey::Private { pubkey, .. } => pubkey,
[460](#460)            DlcKey::Public { pubkey: public } => public,
[461](#461)        }
[462](#462)    }
[463](#463)
[464](#464)    pub fn sign(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 64], DlcError> {
[467](#467)        match self {
[468](#468)            DlcKey::Private { privkey, pubkey } => privkey.with_secret(|seed| {
[469](#469)                let pair = Ed25519KeyPair::from_seed_and_public_key(seed, pubkey.as_ref())
[470](#470)                    .map_err(|e| DlcError::CryptoError(e.to_string()))?;
[471](#471)                let sig = pair.sign(data);
[472](#472)                let mut sig_bytes = [0u8; 64];
[473](#473)                sig_bytes.copy_from_slice(sig.as_ref());
[474](#474)                Ok(sig_bytes)
[475](#475)            }),
[476](#476)            DlcKey::Public { .. } => Err(DlcError::PrivateKeyRequired),
[477](#477)        }
[478](#478)    }
[479](#479)
[480](#480)    pub fn verify(&self, data: &[u8], signature: &[u8; 64]) -> Result<(), DlcError> {
[482](#482)        let pubkey = self.get_public_key();
[483](#483)        ring::signature::UnparsedPublicKey::new(&ring::signature::ED25519, pubkey.as_ref())
[484](#484)            .verify(data, signature.as_ref())
[485](#485)            .map_err(|_| DlcError::SignatureInvalid)
[486](#486)    }

[488](#488)    pub fn create_signed_license<D>(
[494](#494)        &self,
[495](#495)        dlcs: impl IntoIterator<Item = D>,
[496](#496)        product: Product,
[497](#497)    ) -> Result<SignedLicense, DlcError>
[498](#498)    where
[499](#499)        D: std::fmt::Display,
[500](#500)    {
[501](#501)        let mut payload = serde_json::Map::new();
[502](#502)        payload.insert(
[503](#503)            "dlcs".to_string(),
[504](#504)            serde_json::Value::Array(
[505](#505)                dlcs.into_iter()
[506](#506)                    .map(|s| serde_json::Value::String(s.to_string()))
[507](#507)                    .collect(),
[508](#508)            ),
[509](#509)        );
[510](#510)
[511](#511)        payload.insert(
[512](#512)            "product".to_string(),
[513](#513)            serde_json::Value::String(product.as_ref().to_string()),
[514](#514)        );
[515](#515)
[516](#516)        match self {
[517](#517)            DlcKey::Private { privkey, .. } => {
[518](#518)                let sig_token = privkey.with_secret(
[519](#519)                    |encrypt_key_bytes| -> Result<SignedLicense, DlcError> {
[520](#520)                        payload.insert(
[521](#521)                            "encrypt_key".to_string(),
[522](#522)                            serde_json::Value::String(URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(encrypt_key_bytes)),
[523](#523)                        );
[524](#524)
[525](#525)                        let payload_value = serde_json::Value::Object(payload);
[526](#526)                        let payload_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&payload_value)
[527](#527)                            .map_err(|e| DlcError::TokenCreationFailed(e.to_string()))?;
[528](#528)
[529](#529)                        let sig = self.sign(&payload_bytes)?;
[530](#530)                        Ok(SignedLicense::from(format!(
[531](#531)                            "{}.{}",
[532](#532)                            URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(&payload_bytes),
[533](#533)                            URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(sig.as_ref())
[534](#534)                        )))
[535](#535)                    },
[536](#536)                )?;
[537](#537)                Ok(sig_token)
[538](#538)            }
[539](#539)            DlcKey::Public { .. } => Err(DlcError::PrivateKeyRequired),
[540](#540)        }
[541](#541)    }

[543](#543)    pub fn extend_signed_license<D>(
[569](#569)        &self,
[570](#570)        existing: &SignedLicense,
[571](#571)        new_dlcs: impl IntoIterator<Item = D>,
[572](#572)        product: Product,
[573](#573)    ) -> Result<SignedLicense, DlcError>
[574](#574)    where
[575](#575)        D: std::fmt::Display,
[576](#576)    {
[577](#577)        let mut combined_dlcs: Vec<String> = existing.with_secret(|token_str| {
[578](#578)            let parts: Vec<&str> = token_str.split('.').collect();
[579](#579)            if parts.len() != 2 {
[580](#580)                return Vec::new();
[581](#581)            }
[582](#582)            if let Ok(payload) = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(parts[0].as_bytes()) {
[583](#583)                if let Ok(payload_json) = serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&payload) {
[584](#584)                    if let Some(dlcs_array) = payload_json.get("dlcs").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {
[585](#585)                        let mut dlcs = Vec::new();
[586](#586)                        for dlc in dlcs_array {
[587](#587)                            if let Some(dlc_id) = dlc.as_str() {
[588](#588)                                dlcs.push(dlc_id.to_string());
[589](#589)                            }
[590](#590)                        }
[591](#591)                        return dlcs;
[592](#592)                    }
[593](#593)                }
[594](#594)            }
[595](#595)            Vec::new()
[596](#596)        });
[597](#597)
[598](#598)        for new_dlc in new_dlcs {
[599](#599)            let dlc_str = new_dlc.to_string();
[600](#600)            if !combined_dlcs.contains(&dlc_str) {
[601](#601)                combined_dlcs.push(dlc_str);
[602](#602)            }
[603](#603)        }
[604](#604)
[605](#605)        self.create_signed_license(combined_dlcs, product)
[606](#606)    }

[608](#608)    pub fn verify_signed_license(&self, license: &SignedLicense) -> bool {
[614](#614)        license.with_secret(|full_token| {
[615](#615)            let parts: Vec<&str> = full_token.split('.').collect();
[616](#616)            if parts.len() != 2 {
[617](#617)                return false;
[618](#618)            }
[619](#619)
[620](#620)            let payload = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(parts[0]);
[621](#621)            let sig_bytes = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(parts[1]);
[622](#622)            if payload.is_err() || sig_bytes.is_err() {
[623](#623)                return false;
[624](#624)            }
[625](#625)            let payload = payload.unwrap();
[626](#626)            let sig_bytes = sig_bytes.unwrap();
[627](#627)
[628](#628)            if sig_bytes.len() != 64 {
[629](#629)                return false;
[630](#630)            }
[631](#631)
[632](#632)            let public = self.get_public_key().0;
[633](#633)            let public_key = UnparsedPublicKey::new(&ED25519, public);
[634](#634)            public_key.verify(&payload, &sig_bytes).is_ok()
[635](#635)        })
[636](#636)    }

# bevy_dlc::encrypt_key_registry - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/encrypt_key_registry/index.html

## Expand description

Registry for encrypt keys and DLC asset paths. This tracks which encrypt key is associated with which DLC id, and which asset paths are associated with which DLC id so that they can be reloaded when the DLC is unlocked.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [DlcEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.DlcEntry.html)
- Result of a lookup in the registry.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [asset_](https://docs.rs/fn.asset_path_for.html)- path_ - for
- Return the registered asset path for a given `dlc_id`. This is used by the asset loader to determine if a DLC pack file has already been registered for a given DLC ID, which allows it to avoid registering/loading the same pack multiple times. Returns Some(path) if a path is registered, None otherwise.
- [get](https://docs.rs/fn.get.html)
- Return an owned [EncryptionKey](https://docs.rs/type.EncryptionKey.html)(cloned) if present. The clone is performed within the secure closure to minimize exposure time.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_from_path.html)- from_ - path
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_full.html)- full
- Return both the key and the registered path for a given `dlc_id`.
- [insert](https://docs.rs/fn.insert.html)
- Insert or replace the encrypt key for `dlc_id`.
- [iter_](https://docs.rs/fn.iter_ids.html)- ids
- Helper for systems to see all registered DLC IDs.
- [register_](https://docs.rs/fn.register_asset_path.html)- asset_ - path
- Register an asset path for a given `dlc_id`. Each DLC ID can only have ONE associated pack file. This enforces the design constraint that each DLC release is shipped as a single .dlcpack.
- [remove](https://docs.rs/fn.remove.html)
- Remove the encrypt key for `dlc_id`.

# dlc_register_types in bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/macro.dlc_register_types.html

```
macro_rules! dlc_register_types {
    ($app:expr, $($ty:ty),* $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Calls `App::register_dlc_type::<T>()` for each given type on the provided
Bevy `App` instance.

Useful when registering several DLC-supported asset types in one line:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_dlc::prelude::*;
let mut app = App::new();
// an `AssetPlugin` (or AssetLoaders for the asset types) must be added before registering
// asset types; this mirrors real usage inside a Bevy application.
app.add_plugins(AssetPlugin::default());
// bring the `AppExt` trait into scope so the generated calls resolve
dlc_register_types!(app, Image, Mesh);
```

# dlc_simple_asset in bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/macro.dlc_simple_asset.html

```
macro_rules! dlc_simple_asset {
    ($name:ident, $loader:ident, $plugin:ident, $($ext:expr),+ $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Defines a simple “text-like” asset type along with a loader and a Bevy
plugin for it.  The generated loader reads the file as UTF-8 and stores a
`String` in the asset.  The plugin registers the loader and the DLC type.

This is the same pattern used throughout the repository for example assets
(see `examples/mod.rs`) and in the test helpers.  Rather than copy/paste the
struct/loader/plugin boilerplate each time, this macro generates it for you.

The macro takes explicit identifiers for the asset struct, its loader, and
the plugin; this avoids any need for identifier concatenation in
`macro_rules!`.

Parameters:

- `$name`: identifier for the new asset struct.
- `$loader`: identifier for the asset/loader type.
- `$plugin`: identifier for the plugin struct.
- `$($ext:expr),+`: one or more file extensions the loader will recognise.

Example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// demonstration only; we don't actually run a Bevy app inside the doctest
use bevy::prelude::AssetApp;
use bevy_dlc::dlc_simple_asset;
dlc_simple_asset!(TextAsset, TextAssetLoader, TextAssetPlugin, "txt", "text");
```

# include_dlc_key_and_license_aes in bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/macro.include_dlc_key_and_license_aes.html

```
macro_rules! include_dlc_key_and_license_aes {
    ($pubkey_path:expr, $license_path:expr, $license_key:expr $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Includes a secure license token and a public key from files.

Returns a `(DlcKey, SignedLicense)` tuple.

Example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use bevy_dlc::prelude::*;
let (dlc_key, signed_license) = include_dlc_key_and_license_aes!(
    "examples/example_keys/example.pubkey",
    "examples/example_keys/example.slicense",
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ012345", // Don't use a key like this in production! This is just an example for testing purposes. The key must be exactly 32 characters for AES-256.
);
```

# include_signed_license_aes in bevy_dlc - Rust

`include_signed_license_aes!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

# pack_items in bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/macro.pack_items.html

```
macro_rules! pack_items {
    (
        $(
            $path:expr => $bytes:expr
            $(; ext=$ext:expr)?
            $(; type=$type_path:expr)?
        ),* $(,)?
    ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Builds a `Vec<PackItem>` from a list of entries.  Each entry specifies a
path and its raw contents; optional query-style suffixes allow specifying an
explicit original extension or a type path as well.

Examples:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use bevy_dlc::pack_items;
let items = pack_items![
    "note.txt" => b"hello",
    // override the extension that would otherwise be inferred
    "other" => b"data"; ext="bin",
    // supply a type path to help the runtime choose a loader (optional)
    "model" => b"objdata"; type="bevy::gltf::Gltf",
];
```

### impl<T> [ConditionalSend](https://docs.rs/bevy_tasks/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_tasks/trait.ConditionalSend.html) for T

Converts

# DlcPackLoader in bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/struct.DlcPackLoader.html

```
pub struct DlcPackLoader {
    pub registrars:
```
[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn ErasedSubAssetRegistrar>>,
    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

`AssetLoader` for `.dlcpack` bundles (contains multiple encrypted entries).

When the encrypt key is available in the registry at load time (i.e. the
DLC is already unlocked), each entry is immediately decrypted and registered
as a typed labeled sub-asset so `asset_server.load("pack.dlcpack#entry.png")`
returns the correct `Handle<T>` for the extension’s loader (e.g. `Handle<Image>`
for `.png`). No asset type is hardcoded here — the correct type is determined
purely by extension dispatch via Bevy’s `immediate()` loader, and the result
is downcast + registered using the list of `ErasedSubAssetRegistrar`s that
`DlcPlugin::build` populates.

When the encrypt key is *not* yet available the pack is still loaded
successfully (entries list is populated from the manifest) but the labeled
sub-assets are not added — `reload_assets_on_unlock_system` will reload the
pack once the key arrives, and the second load will succeed.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.registrars)

`registrars: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn ErasedSubAssetRegistrar>>Ordered list of per-type registrars. `DlcPlugin::build` pushes one
`TypedSubAssetRegistrar<A>` for every `A` it also registers via
`init_asset_loader::<DlcLoader<A>>()`. The loader tries each in turn
and uses the first successful downcast.

# DlcPlugin in bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/struct.DlcPlugin.html

`pub struct DlcPlugin { /* private fields */ }`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Has the plugin finished its setup? This can be useful for plugins that need something
asynchronous to happen before they can finish their setup, like the initialization of a renderer.
Once the plugin is ready,

[should be called.](https://docs.rs/bevy_app/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_app/plugin/trait.Plugin.html#method.finish)`finish`Runs after all plugins are built and finished, but before the app schedule is executed.
This can be useful if you have some resource that other plugins need during their build step,
but after build you want to remove it and send it to another thread.

}## Expand description

Represents a single encrypted file inside a `.dlcpack` container, along with its metadata (DLC ID, original extension, optional type path). The ciphertext is not decrypted at this stage; decryption is performed on demand by `DlcPackEntry::decrypt_bytes` using the global encrypt key registry.

# CompressionLevel in bevy_dlc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy-dlc/1.19.0/bevy_dlc/enum.CompressionLevel.html

```
pub enum CompressionLevel {
    Fast,
    Default,
    Best,
}
```
## Expand description

Compression level for packing. Controls the trade-off between pack size and packing time. Higher levels produce smaller files but take longer to create. TODO: v6 format will allow a pack to contain multiple blocks with different compression levels, because some file types compress better than others.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fast)

### Fast

Fast compression (level 1), suitable for rapid iterations

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Default)

### Default

Balanced compression (level 6, default), good trade-off

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Best)

### Best

Best compression (level 9), smallest file size for distribution

Parse a `.dlcpack` container and return product, embedded dlc_id, and a list
of `(path, EncryptedAsset)` pairs. For v3 format, also validates the signature
against the authorized product public key.

Returns: (product, dlc_id, entries, signature_bytes_if_v3)

### TokenProductMismatch

The DLC pack being loaded is cryptographically valid but the product it is bound to does not match the expected product. This indicates a mismatch between the pack and the game’s registered product key.

The version of the pack being loaded is older than the minimum supported version. The string contains the minimum supported version (e.g. “3”).

}## Expand description

Client-side wrapper for Ed25519 key operations: verify tokens and (when private) create compact signed tokens.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

Private key (protected seed + public bytes + public key tag)

Public-only key (public bytes)

#### pub fn [extend_signed_license](https://docs.rs#method.extend_signed_license)<D>(
    &self,
    existing: &[SignedLicense](https://docs.rs/type.SignedLicense.html),
    new_dlcs: impl [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)<Item = D>,
    product: [Product](https://docs.rs/struct.Product.html),
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/bevy_ecs/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_ecs/error/type.Result.html)<[SignedLicense](https://docs.rs/type.SignedLicense.html), [DlcError](https://docs.rs/enum.DlcError.html)>

Extend an existing signed license by merging additional DLC ids while preserving backwards compatibility.

Extracts the DLC ids from an existing (unsigned or unverified) license payload, merges them with the provided new DLC ids (with deduplication), and creates a fresh signed license with the combined list. The product must match this key’s current product.

**Important**: This creates a NEW signed token with a potentially different signature,
but the payload contains all previous DLC ids plus the new ones. Existing DLC packs
remain unlocked by the new license.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use bevy_dlc::{DlcKey, SignedLicense, Product};
// in a real program you would obtain a key and product from your build
// process or configuration.  we use simple constructors here so the
// example compiles without panicking.
let dlc_key: DlcKey = DlcKey::generate_random();
let product: Product = Product::from("my_game");
let old_license = SignedLicense::from("...existing token...");
let _new_license = dlc_key
    .extend_signed_license(&old_license, &["new_expansion"], product)
    .unwrap();
```

#### fn [register_dlc_type](https://docs.rs#tymethod.register_dlc_type)<T: [Asset](https://docs.rs/bevy_asset/0.19.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bevy_asset/trait.Asset.html)>(&mut self) -> &mut Self

Register a `DlcLoader` for the given asset type `T`. This is required for any asset type
that may be loaded from a DLC pack. The plugin registers loaders for common asset types
(Image, Scene, Mesh, Font, AudioSource, etc.) but you must register loaders for any custom
asset types.

**Important**: As of `v2.0`, this function also calls `init_asset::<T>()` to register the asset type itself, so you do not need to call `init_asset` separately.

**Suggestion**: If I missed a common asset type that should be supported out-of-the-box,
please open an issue or PR to add it!

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*
